import pandas as pd

# Define source file paths
source_files = [
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length4_89/training_0.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length4_89/training_1.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length4_89/training_2.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length4_89/training_3.csv"
]

# Load all source tables into a list of DataFrames
dfs = []
for file_path in source_files:
    df = pd.read_csv(file_path, index_col=0)
    dfs.append(df)

# According to operation_history: UNION of all source tables
# All source tables have the same schema, so union is valid
# We only need the 'video' column for the target table
union_df = pd.concat(dfs, ignore_index=True)

# Project only the 'video' column as per target schema
target_df = union_df[['video']].copy()

# Remove duplicate rows if any (not explicitly stated but usually good practice)
# The target examples show distinct rows, but prompt does not forbid duplicates
# So we keep duplicates as is to strictly follow instructions

# Write the result to the target path
target_df.to_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length4_89/target_multisource.csv", index=False)
